intro: Assemble PDF is a workbench for building documents out of other documents. Every PDF or image you add shows up as a column with its pages, and you move pages from one column to another until you have the documents you need: separating several clients' invoices that arrived in one scan, putting an application together with a photo of an ID card or rebuilding a case file from pages of several files.

Drag a page to move it within its column or into another one; if you would rather not drag, the “Move to…” menu sends it to the end of the document you pick. Each page has buttons to rotate it 90°, duplicate it or delete it. “New document” adds an empty column to fill, and each column's name, which you can edit, becomes the PDF's name.

It takes PDFs and photos in JPG, PNG, WEBP, GIF and BMP. JPG and PNG are embedded without recompression; the others are turned into PNG, losslessly. Each image becomes a page of its own size, counting 96 pixels per inch.

When you press “Save the documents”, every column with pages becomes a PDF; if there is more than one, you can also download them all in a ZIP. Everything happens in your browser: neither the documents nor the images leave your device.

faq.q: How is it different from Merge PDF?
faq.a: Merge PDF joins whole files into one. Assemble PDF works page by page and can produce several documents at once, each with the pages you choose.
No. PDF pages are copied as they are, and rotating only changes their orientation without redrawing them.

faq.q: Can I use a password-protected PDF?
faq.a: The board does not open protected files. Remove the password first with Unlock PDF and then add the file.
